The MINISFORUM MS-A2 is a mini workstation built for homelab, virtualization, and high-throughput networking, available with the AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX, Ryzen 9 8945HX, Ryzen 9 7945HX, or Ryzen 7 7745HX. The flagship Ryzen 9 9955HX is a Zen 5 processor with 16 cores, 32 threads, 64MB of L3 cache, a maximum boost clock of 5.4 GHz, and a 100W turbo TDP
column2:
the Ryzen 9 7945HX offers the same core count and boost clock on the Zen 4 architecture. What defines the MS-A2 is the combination of features it fits into a 1.78-litre chassis: two 10Gbps SFP+ ports, two 2.5GbE RJ45 ports, three NVMe storage positions with U.2 enterprise SSD support, and a physical PCIe x16 slot with bandwidth splitting. At 196 × 189 × 48 mm and 1.4 kg, with a lightweight metal structure and non-slip base pads, it delivers desktop-class core counts in a footprint that fits on a shelf or inside a cabinet.

The MS-A2 supports up to 96GB of DDR5 memory across two SO-DIMM slots, running at DDR5-5600 with Ryzen 9000 series processors and DDR5-5200 with Ryzen 7000 series, delivering 89.6 GB/s of memory bandwidth against 51.2 GB/s for dual-channel DDR4-3200, with memory latency reduced to roughly 80 ns. Storage is arranged across three positions: one M.2 2280 slot that also accepts U.2 NVMe drives at PCIe 4.0 x4, supporting enterprise SSDs up to 15TB, and two M.2 2280 or 22110 slots supporting up to 4TB each. The two secondary slots default to PCIe 3.0 x4 and can be switched to PCIe 4.0 x4 in the BIOS, which is worth checking after installation since the default setting halves available bandwidth. Consumer configurations reach 12TB total at up to 7000 MB/s per drive
column3:
adding a 15TB U.2 enterprise drive raises maximum capacity to 23TB. RAID 0 and RAID 1 are supported, with RAID 0 transfer speeds reaching 13,000 MB/s.

Networking on the MS-A2 combines two 10Gbps SFP+ ports driven by an Intel X710 controller with two 2.5GbE RJ45 ports, one using a Realtek RTL8125 controller and one using an Intel I226-V controller. Four independent interfaces allow WAN, LAN, DMZ, and management segmentation on a single device, which is what makes the system practical as a firewall appliance or as a virtualization node with separate storage and client networks. Using two different 2.5GbE controllers also helps in environments where driver support differs between operating systems, since one interface is likely to work even if the other needs attention. The built-in expansion slot is physically PCIe x16 with PCIe 4.0 x8 bandwidth, and it supports splitting into two PCIe 4.0 x4 links, so a single slot can carry either one graphics or accelerator card or two separate expansion cards, such as an additional network adapter alongside a storage controller. Wireless is Wi-Fi 6E with Bluetooth.

Graphics are handled by the integrated AMD Radeon 610M running at 2200 MHz, which is sufficient for multi-display administration, console work, and general desktop use while leaving heavier graphics tasks to a card installed in the PCIe slot. Buyers should note that the 610M is a basic integrated GPU rather than a Radeon 890M-class part, so this system is not intended for gaming or GPU-accelerated rendering without an add-in card. Rear connectivity includes two USB-C ports at USB 3.2 Gen2 speeds with DisplayPort 2.0 Alt Mode supporting up to 8K at 60Hz or 4K at 144Hz, one HDMI 2.1 port supporting up to 8K at 60Hz, one USB 3.2 Gen2 Type-A port, and one USB 3.2 Gen1 Type-A port. The front panel carries two USB 3.2 Gen1 ports, one USB 2.0 port, and a 3.5mm combo jack. Cooling uses a triple pure-copper heat pipe architecture, phase change material, and a turbine fan with aerodynamic vortex grooves that increases system airflow by 30 percent. Power comes from a 19V/12.63A external adapter, and the system ships with Windows 11.

Common use cases for the MINISFORUM MS-A2 include Proxmox and VMware virtualization hosts where 16 cores and 96GB of DDR5 support more than 20 concurrent virtual machines, pfSense and OPNsense firewall appliances using the four segmented network interfaces, TrueNAS and ZFS storage nodes that pair a 15TB U.2 enterprise SSD with consumer NVMe drives, Kubernetes and LXC container labs needing high thread counts for workload density, software compilation and CI runners, and 10GbE workgroup file serving for video production. Buyers typically choose the MS-A2 over the Intel-based MS-01 when they want 32 threads instead of 20 and a splittable PCIe slot, and accept Radeon 610M graphics and Wi-Fi 6E in exchange. Buyers needing copper 10GBASE-T should note that the 10Gbps ports here are SFP+ and require a compatible transceiver module or DAC cable
column4: the MS-03 and M2 Pro provide copper 10GbE on RJ45 instead. Buyers needing more than two memory slots should look at the MS-02 Ultra.

The flagship Ryzen 9 9955HX is a Zen 5 processor with 16 cores, 32 threads, 64MB of L3 cache, a maximum boost clock of 5.4 GHz, and a 100W turbo TDP
column2:
the Ryzen 9 7945HX offers the same core count and boost clock on the Zen 4 architecture. What defines the MS-A2 is the combination of features it fits into a 1.78-litre chassis: two 10Gbps SFP+ ports, two 2.5GbE RJ45 ports, three NVMe storage positions with U.2 enterprise SSD support, and a physical PCIe x16 slot with bandwidth splitting. At 196 × 189 × 48 mm and 1.4 kg, with a lightweight metal structure and non-slip base pads, it delivers desktop-class core counts in a footprint that fits on a shelf or inside a cabinet.

The MS-A2 supports up to 96GB of DDR5 memory across two SO-DIMM slots, running at DDR5-5600 with Ryzen 9000 series processors and DDR5-5200 with Ryzen 7000 series, delivering 89.6 GB/s of memory bandwidth against 51.2 GB/s for dual-channel DDR4-3200, with memory latency reduced to roughly 80 ns. Storage is arranged across three positions: one M.2 2280 slot that also accepts U.2 NVMe drives at PCIe 4.0 x4, supporting enterprise SSDs up to 15TB, and two M.2 2280 or 22110 slots supporting up to 4TB each. The two secondary slots default to PCIe 3.0 x4 and can be switched to PCIe 4.0 x4 in the BIOS, which is worth checking after installation since the default setting halves available bandwidth. Consumer configurations reach 12TB total at up to 7000 MB/s per drive
column3:
adding a 15TB U.2 enterprise drive raises maximum capacity to 23TB. RAID 0 and RAID 1 are supported, with RAID 0 transfer speeds reaching 13,000 MB/s.

The MINISFORUM AI X1 Pro-470 is a Copilot+ AI mini PC powered by the AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470, a 12-core, 24-thread processor with a maximum turbo frequency of 5.2 GHz. Its NPU delivers up to 55 TOPS, while total system AI performance reaches up to 86 TOPS. The 55 TOPS NPU sits well above the 40 TOPS Microsoft requires for Copilot+ certification, which means AI writing assistance, summarization, translation, and lightweight local inference run on-device rather than waiting in a cloud queue. The system supports up to 128GB of DDR5 memory, three M.2 PCIe 4.0 NVMe slots totalling 12TB, dual USB4 ports, and an OCuLink port for external GPU expansion. A built-in 134.9W power supply removes the external brick and keeps a single cable to the desk, and a fingerprint reader adds Windows Hello sign-in. The chassis measures 195 × 195 × 42.5 to 47.5 mm and weighs 1.5 kg, and the system ships with Windows 11 Pro. Factory configurations run from barebone through 96GB of memory with a 2TB drive.

The AI X1 Pro-470 accepts up to 128GB of DDR5 memory across two SO-DIMM slots at a maximum speed of 5600 MHz. Because memory is user-replaceable rather than soldered, capacity can be raised after purchase, which matters for local AI work where the size of model you can load is bounded by installed memory, and which also gives buyers a hedge against DDR5 price volatility by starting small and upgrading later. Storage consists of three M.2 2280 NVMe slots: two running at PCIe 4.0 x4 and one at PCIe 4.0 x1, each supporting drives up to 4TB, for 12TB of total capacity. The three-slot layout allows a separate boot drive, an active project or scratch drive, and a library or archive drive inside one chassis, with the x1 slot best suited to the archive role since its bandwidth is a fraction of the x4 slots. An SD card reader is built into the side of the system for direct media import without an external reader.

Graphics are handled by the integrated AMD Radeon 890M, which handles light to mid-weight gaming and accelerates creative workflows without a discrete card. For users who need more, the OCuLink port provides a direct PCIe connection to an external GPU dock and delivers substantially higher bandwidth and lower latency than a USB4 or Thunderbolt enclosure, which is the practical difference when running CUDA workloads or gaming at higher frame rates
column2:
MINISFORUM quotes roughly 90 percent of native eGPU performance over this connection. Display output covers four simultaneous 4K screens through one HDMI 2.1 FRL port, one DisplayPort 2.0 port, and two USB4 ports, with the HDMI and DisplayPort outputs each supporting up to 8K at 60Hz or 4K at 120Hz. This native port layout removes the need for docks or hubs in a multi-monitor setup, which is a meaningful difference for trading desks and editing suites where a hub adds both latency and a failure point.

Connectivity includes two 2.5 Gigabit RJ45 Ethernet ports, Wi-Fi 7 with Bluetooth 5.4, two USB 3.2 Gen2 Type-A ports, one USB 2.0 Type-A port, and two USB4 ports. The rear USB4 port supports 65W to 100W Power Delivery input as well as 15W output, while the front USB4 port provides 15W output. The system includes dual noise-cancelling digital microphones, two built-in speakers, a 3.5mm combo jack, a fingerprint reader supporting Windows Hello, a dedicated Copilot button, a Kensington lock slot, and an SD card slot, so meetings and secure sign-in need no external peripherals. Cooling uses a three-tier architecture combining phase change material, dual copper heat pipes, and active airflow: under full load the CPU stabilizes below 80°C with idle temperatures around 37°C, and noise stays below 45 dB at a typical 42 dB, quiet enough to leave running overnight on a long inference or rendering job. Power is supplied by an internal 19V/7.1A 134.9W adapter accepting 100 to 240V AC input.

Common use cases for the MINISFORUM AI X1 Pro-470 include on-device Copilot+ AI tasks such as writing assistance, summarization, live captions, Recall, and translation, running local language models and lightweight inference through Ollama or LM Studio, video editing and asset work using three separate NVMe drives for project, cache, and library storage, four-display productivity and trading setups driven natively without a dock, meeting and conference use through the built-in dual microphones and speakers, and light to mid-weight gaming on the Radeon 890M with an OCuLink eGPU upgrade path available later. Buyers typically choose the AI X1 Pro-470 over the AI X1 Pro-370 for its higher 55 TOPS NPU performance, up to 86 TOPS of total system AI performance, and 5.2 GHz turbo clock, and over a Strix Halo system such as the MS-S1 MAX when upgradeable SO-DIMM memory and three NVMe slots matter more than unified memory bandwidth. Buyers needing 10GbE networking or PCIe expansion should look at the MS-03 or MS-A2 instead.

The MINISFORUM MS-03 is a mini workstation available in two configurations: the MS-03-S386H with an Intel Core Ultra 9 386H providing 16 cores and 16 threads at 1.6 to 4.9 GHz with PL1 at 70W and PL2 at 80W in Balance mode, and the MS-03-S336H with an Intel Core Ultra 5 336H providing 12 cores and 12 threads at 1.5 to 4.6 GHz at 65W. Both processors carry Intel vPro for BIOS-level remote management. The MS-03 combines four network interfaces including two 10 Gigabit SFP+ ports and one 10 Gigabit RJ45 port, PCIe 5.0 storage, a half-height PCIe expansion slot, and a 50 TOPS NPU on the 386H, in a 196 × 189 × 48 mm chassis weighing 1.4 kg. It is the first MINISFORUM workstation in this form factor to carry both copper and fibre 10 Gigabit networking on the same board, which removes the transceiver requirement that applies to the MS-01 and MS-A2.

The MS-03 uses two DDR5 SO-DIMM slots supporting up to 128GB of memory, with factory configurations at 32GB and 64GB and supported speeds of 5600, 6400, and 7200 MT/s. Storage is where the MS-03 differs most from earlier models sharing this chassis: two of its M.2 slots run at PCIe 5.0 x4 rather than PCIe 4.0, supporting drives up to 8TB each, with one accepting 2280 drives and one accepting 2280 or 22110 lengths. A third M.2 2280 or 22110 slot runs at PCIe 4.0 x1, also supporting up to 8TB. U.2 enterprise SSDs up to 15TB are supported through an adapter. PCIe 5.0 doubles the per-drive bandwidth ceiling over PCIe 4.0, which matters for storage arrays, database workloads, and video ingest where a single NVMe drive would otherwise become the bottleneck before the network or the CPU does. The 22110 slot length also accommodates the longer enterprise drives that many datacentre NVMe models ship in.

The MS-03 carries four network interfaces: one 10 Gigabit RJ45 port using a Realtek RTL8127 controller, one 2.5 Gigabit RJ45 port using an Intel i226-LM controller with vPro support, and two 10 Gigabit SFP+ ports using an Intel X710 controller. Having both copper 10GBASE-T and SFP+ on the same system means it can connect directly to a copper 10GbE switch with no transceiver while still supporting fibre or DAC connections to a separate storage network, a combination the MS-01 and MS-A2 do not offer and which removes a common reason to add a PCIe network card. A half-height PCIe x16 slot with PCIe 4.0 x4 bandwidth accepts cards up to 170 mm long and 20 mm thick, leaving that slot free for a storage controller or accelerator instead. Wireless is Wi-Fi 7 via an Intel BE211 module with Bluetooth 6, and vPro on the 2.5GbE interface allows out-of-band management even when the operating system is unresponsive.

Graphics on the MS-03-S386H run at 2.5 GHz and deliver 40 TOPS Int8, with a separate NPU rated at 50 TOPS Int8
column2:

The rear adds two USB 3.2 Gen2 Type-A ports, two USB4 Type-C ports at 40Gbps with DisplayPort 2.1 Alt Mode, one HDMI 2.1 port at 4K 120Hz, and all four network ports. Common use cases for the MINISFORUM MS-03 include Proxmox and Linux virtualization nodes with vPro remote management, pfSense and OPNsense firewall appliances using four segmented network interfaces, TrueNAS and Ceph storage nodes where PCIe 5.0 NVMe and dual 10GbE SFP+ remove the usual bottlenecks, mixed-network deployments needing both copper 10GBASE-T and fibre on one device, Kubernetes lab clusters, Plex and Jellyfin media servers with hardware transcoding, and edge nodes running local AI inference on the 50 TOPS NPU alongside their primary workload. The MS-03 combines four network interfaces including two 10 Gigabit SFP+ ports and one 10 Gigabit RJ45 port, PCIe 5.0 storage, a half-height PCIe expansion slot, and a 50 TOPS NPU on the 386H, in a 196 × 189 × 48 mm chassis weighing 1.4 kg. It is the first MINISFORUM workstation in this form factor to carry both copper and fibre 10 Gigabit networking on the same board, which removes the transceiver requirement that applies to the MS-01 and MS-A2.

The MS-03 uses two DDR5 SO-DIMM slots supporting up to 128GB of memory, with factory configurations at 32GB and 64GB and supported speeds of 5600, 6400, and 7200 MT/s. Storage is where the MS-03 differs most from earlier models sharing this chassis: two of its M.2 slots run at PCIe 5.0 x4 rather than PCIe 4.0, supporting drives up to 8TB each, with one accepting 2280 drives and one accepting 2280 or 22110 lengths. A third M.2 2280 or 22110 slot runs at PCIe 4.0 x1, also supporting up to 8TB. U.2 enterprise SSDs up to 15TB are supported through an adapter. PCIe 5.0 doubles the per-drive bandwidth ceiling over PCIe 4.0, which matters for storage arrays, database workloads, and video ingest where a single NVMe drive would otherwise become the bottleneck before the network or the CPU does. The 22110 slot length also accommodates the longer enterprise drives that many datacentre NVMe models ship in.

The MINISFORUM M2 Pro is a compact AI mini PC powered by the Intel Core Ultra X7 processor 358H, a 16-core processor with a 1.5 GHz base frequency on its performance cores and a maximum turbo of 4.8 GHz. Its defining feature is the graphics subsystem: an Intel Arc B390 GPU with 12 Xe3 cores delivering 122 TOPS of Int8 performance, alongside a 50 TOPS NPU. That GPU figure is unusual in this form factor and shifts most AI inference onto the graphics engine rather than onto the neural processor alone, which suits the llama.cpp and diffusion backends that target GPUs rather than NPUs. The system pairs this with 10 Gigabit Ethernet on copper RJ45, three M.2 NVMe slots totalling up to 24TB, three USB4 ports, and a built-in 134.9W power supply, in a 1.81-litre chassis measuring 195 × 195 × 47.5 mm at 1.39 kg that can sit flat, stand vertically, or mount behind a display.

The M2 Pro uses onboard LPDDR5X memory running at up to 7467 MT/s with a maximum capacity of 32GB. The memory is soldered rather than socketed, which delivers higher bandwidth than SO-DIMM designs at the same generation but fixes capacity at the point of purchase, so buyers should size their configuration for the workloads they intend to run rather than planning to upgrade later. This 32GB ceiling is the single most important constraint on the system and should be weighed before purchase against the AI X1 Pro-370, which reaches 128GB at lower bandwidth. Storage compensates generously with three M.2 2280 slots: two at PCIe 4.0 x4 and one at PCIe 4.0 x1, each supporting drives up to 8TB, for up to 24TB of total NVMe capacity. That is double the per-slot ceiling of most mini PCs in this class, and the three-slot layout allows separate boot, scratch, and archive volumes without external enclosures.

Graphics and AI acceleration on the M2 Pro come from the Intel Arc B390 integrated GPU with 12 Xe3 cores, rated at 122 TOPS Int8, combined with an NPU rated at 50 TOPS Int8. For inference workloads that run on the graphics engine, which includes most llama.cpp and Stable Diffusion backends, the Arc B390 does the heavy lifting while the NPU handles background and low-power AI tasks such as camera effects and Copilot features. Display output supports four simultaneous screens through one HDMI 2.1 FRL port supporting 4K at 144Hz or 8K at 60Hz with CEC, one DisplayPort 1.4 port at 4K 144Hz, and three USB4 ports carrying DisplayPort 2.1 Alt Mode. The 144Hz ceiling on the primary outputs also makes the system usable for high-refresh-rate work and gaming rather than 60Hz office displays only, which is unusual for a mini PC at this size and removes the need for a discrete card in most creative and gaming workloads.

Networking on the M2 Pro combines one 10 Gigabit RJ45 port with one 2.5 Gigabit RJ45 port, plus Intel Wi-Fi 7 via a BE211 module and Bluetooth 6.0. Copper 10GbE on an RJ45 connector is worth noting because it needs no transceiver, unlike the SFP+ ports on the MS-01 and MS-A2, which lowers both cost and setup complexity for buyers with an existing copper switch. The front panel carries one USB4 port at 40Gbps with DisplayPort 2.1 Alt Mode and 15W Power Delivery output, two USB 3.2 Gen2 Type-A ports, and a 3.5mm combo jack. The rear adds two more USB4 ports, one supporting 65W to 100W Power Delivery input, one USB 2.0 port, HDMI, DisplayPort, both LAN ports, a second 3.5mm jack, and a reset hole. An SD card reader, power button, fingerprint sensor, Copilot button, and Kensington lock sit on the right side and top. Cooling uses phase change material with dual heat pipes and a turbo fan at up to 5000 RPM, holding the CPU below 79°C at full load
column2:
noise is 29 to 30 dBA at idle, 31 dBA in Balanced mode under load, and 43.2 dBA in Performance mode.

Common use cases for the MINISFORUM M2 Pro include local AI inference that runs on the graphics engine rather than the NPU, AI image generation drawing on the Arc B390's 122 TOPS, 10GbE workgroup file access over copper without transceivers, video editing and colour work across up to four displays at 144Hz, Docker and container hosts, high-refresh-rate gaming on integrated graphics, and compact desktop replacement builds where a 1.39 kg chassis with an internal power supply stands in for a tower. Buyers typically choose the M2 Pro over an AMD-based mini PC when they want copper 10GbE and strong integrated graphics compute in a single box. The 32GB soldered memory ceiling is the main constraint: workloads needing more than 32GB resident, such as language models above roughly 20B parameters at common quantizations, are better matched to the AI X1 Pro-370 with up to 128GB of SO-DIMM memory, or to an MS-S1 MAX with 128GB of unified memory.
